newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania private Bankcoop bank president resigns.
newsitem.headline: Romania private Bankcoop bank president resigns.

text.p: Romania's private Banca de Credit Cooperatist Bankcoop SA said on Tuesday its president had resigned and its board had accepted the resignation.
"The bank's board approved unanimously the resignation of president Alexandru Dinulescu," a statement from the private bank Bankcoop said.
Vice-president Viorel Olteanu will take over the president's duties, it said.
Bankcoop officials said a shareholders' meeting next month would elect a new Bankcoop president but they declined to comment on the reason behind Dinulescu's resignation.
Dinulescu was not immediately available for comment.
Over the past month, Dinulescu was at the centre of a tit-for-tat with Bankcoop's main shareholder George Paunescu, head of a large media and tourism holding.
Last week the central bank dismissed Dinulescu's allegations saying Paunescu's $10 million capital injection into Bankcoop had been illegal.
Paunescu denied the accusations saying they were "an attempt to cover bad management at the bank".
The row sparked queues at the bank's offices earlier this year when people rushed to withdraw their money, but panic subsided soon.
Bankcoop reported an end-1996 provisional balance sheet of 2.1 trillion lei ($289.9 million), 870 billion lei up from 1995 and a 1996 gross profit of 66 billion ($9.3 million). ($=7,024 lei)
